outline.description: This chapter establishes the factual matrix of the employment dispute, the specific wage and hour statutes involved, and the critical procedural developments regarding the stipulation of payment prior to judgment.
subtopics: Employment relationship: Cohen as hourly licensed attorney document reviewer
The 2019 overtime policy change eliminating premium pay
Statutes invoked: MPWA, MFLSA, and MWTA claims
Remedies sought: Overtime, liquidated damages, penalties, and injunctive relief
Pre-judgment stipulation: Full payment of wages and liquidated damages
District Court's grant of summary judgment to Consilio
Scope of the Eighth Circuit appeal

outline.chapter_title: Statutory Interpretation of the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act (MPWA)
outline.description: This chapter analyzes the court's statutory construction of the MPWA to determine whether an individual employee has the independent right to seek 'average daily wage penalties' or if that authority is reserved for the Commissioner.
subtopics: Textual analysis of Minn. Stat. § 181.101(a) regarding penalties
The Commissioner's exclusive role in serving demand and collecting penalties
Comparison with other MPWA sections (§ 181.13, § 181.14) granting employee penalty rights
Legislative intent: The 'knows how' canon of statutory construction
Precedent on Commissioner enforcement authority (Allan v. R.D. Offutt Co.)
Holding: Employee lacks standing to seek MPWA penalties directly

outline.chapter_title: Jurisdictional Challenges: Standing and Mootness under the MFLSA
outline.description: This chapter examines the complex jurisdictional issues arising from Cohen's MFLSA penalty claim after full payment of wages, focusing on Article III standing, mootness, and the voluntary cessation doctrine.
subtopics: Distinction between private damages and civil penalties payable to the state
Article III standing requirements for citizen plaintiffs (Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw)
Mootness doctrine: Whether payment of wages extinguishes the controversy
The 'voluntary cessation' exception to mootness
The unresolved factual dispute regarding the current overtime policy
Remand instructions: District Court to determine continuing jurisdiction

outline.chapter_title: Waiver, Procedural Default, and Final Disposition
outline.description: This chapter covers the court's handling of the remaining claims, specifically the MWTA notice claim and the injunctive relief request, addressing issues of waiver and procedural timing before stating the final judgment.
subtopics: MWTA claim: Dismissal due to lack of argument or statutory authority (Waiver)
Injunctive relief: Improperly raised in summary judgment briefing rather than complaint
Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(a) and amendment of pleadings
Final disposition: Affirm in part (MPWA, MWTA, Injunction), Vacate and Remand in part (MFLSA)
Special Concurrence: Judge Kobes' concerns on standing and attorney's fees
